description: 6 pages. Page 1: cover (28/16/12pt centered title lines) with the 9pt line "© 2026 Course Pack — All rights reserved". Page 2: table of contents ("Contents" 16pt, 11pt dot-leader entries including "References ........ 6"). Page 3: 14pt headings "Introduction" and a mid-document "Notes" (page 3 of 6, before 60% of the document). Pages 4-5: 14pt headings "Results", "Discussion" with body text. Page 6: a body paragraph, then a 14pt "References" heading followed by 10pt APA entries with an 18pt hanging indent. No running headers or footers.
format: Per page: `lines` = expected buildLines(page).map(l => l.text) in reading order; `spoken` = text to speak with DEFAULT_FILTERS; `spokenReadEverything` = text to speak with READ_EVERYTHING; `skipped` = what DEFAULT_FILTERS drop. Spoken text joins lines with single spaces, de-hyphenates "-" + lowercase line starts, and is normalized (ligatures expanded, soft hyphens removed, NBSP/thin space -> space).
notes: Page 1 is skipped by default as a cover/copyright page (© / "all rights reserved" / "course pack" markers).

Page 2 (contents) is spoken by default: the spec has no table-of-contents filter, it has no cover markers, and it has more than 2 sentences. Its "References ........ 6" line must NOT stop reading (not a standalone heading; page 2 of 6).
The page 3 "Notes" heading is a standalone heading-sized line but lies before the last 40% of the document, so it must NOT stop reading.
Speech stops at the page 6 "References" heading (last 40% of the document): the heading and everything after it are not spoken by default.

benefit was largest for students who answered the questions without looking back at the text.
